newsitem.title: JAPAN: LDP URGES STIFFER PENALTIES FOR FINANCIAL MISDEEDS.
newsitem.headline: LDP URGES STIFFER PENALTIES FOR FINANCIAL MISDEEDS.

text.p: The ruling Liberal Democratic Party on Monday unveiled a package of measures to curb financial scandals with stiffer fines and prison sentences for racketeering, fraud and other illegal activities.

The plan by a special LDP investigative committee -- formed in response to the racketeer payoff scandal which has engulfed Nomura Securities, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank and Yamaichi Securities -- would more than double current penalties for the crimes.
The scheme, which also obligates financial firms to report racketeers' threats, would go to parliament for deliberation and ratification in the autumn session, an LDP official said.
The measures take aim at "sokaiya" racketeers, who buy shares in firms and try to extort money from them by threatening to expose dubious business practices.
Firms that hired sokaiya to hush up questions by legitimate shareholders would also face stiffer penalties.

Those convicted of giving or receiving payments to prevent disruption of shareholders' meetings -- sokaiya practices at the heart of the unfolding scandal -- would face a jail term of up to five years and fines of up to five million yen, up from one year and 500,000 yen, the LDP said.

Those convicted of giving special favours to shareholders -- compensation for losses or other payments -- or receiving such treatment would face a jail term of up to three years and fines of up to three million yen, up from the current six months and 300,000 yen.

A special breach of trust, which would apply to company officials who make outright illegal payments, would be penalised with up to 10 years in jail and fines of up to 10 million yen, up from seven years and three million yen at present.

Evading investigations by financial authorities or filing false reports would draw a jail sentence of up to one year and a fine of up to three million yen for individuals, while firms would be fined up to 200 million yen for those offences.
The LDP's planned Commercial Code revisions would also make it a crime for sokaiya to merely request payments. Current law makes only actual the exchange of funds illegal.
The measures also call for making it a legal obligation for executives to report sokaiya demands for payments to authorities.
